status: Design concept, not runtime evidence or approved implementation
initial_prompt:
Create a refined Starfall game environment design comparison, showing PHONE PORTRAIT at left and IPAD LANDSCAPE at right, both in the same moonlit Observatory setting. Use the supplied CURRENT native game captures as references for the painterly violet moonstone, brass telescope, clouds, lantern, expressive five-colored star characters and open floor. They show the problem to correct: floating black UI cards and ungrounded top controls. This deliverable is a DESIGN CONCEPT, not an implementation screenshot. One wide image, with the entire portrait view visible and a larger entire landscape view visible, modest gutter between them, tiny clear labels "Phone portrait" and "iPad landscape". No device hardware or thick external frames.

Critical design correction: UI GROOVES ARE PHYSICAL ARCHITECTURE OF THE ENVIRONMENT. The score/control area is a shallow scooped groove in a moonstone-and-brass UPPER LEDGE. The portrait/message/actions area is a curved LOWER SHELF or hollow carved into the actual front apron of the same playable platform. Their material, thickness, lighting, shadows, wear and physical joins must visibly continue into the arena's stonework and surrounding props. The recess is defined by real bevels, lip thickness and cast shadows. It must NOT look like a rounded rectangle/card overlaid on a painting, a floating plaque, a separate window, a speech bubble, or a decorative bezel around a dark software panel. No black/navy solid rectangle anywhere. The inner floor of each recess is matte muted lavender moonstone, darker through physical shade rather than a flat UI fill, with quiet space for native text. Organically curved edges, restrained craft, asymmetric little chips, NOT a rigid squared-off frame or ornate cage around all four screen edges. Keep plentiful open sky and clouds.

Phone composition: natural upper curved shelf with a small score cavity left (a star icon and "0"), and two shallow button depressions on the right for swap/menu symbols. A slim incised strip immediately below it can hold a short phase cue "Dusk · 5 showers". The telescope remains a separate real interactive prop near the back-left outside the arena. The central platform remains the dominant open uninterrupted 7x7 playfield: 49 actual star pieces arranged in seven rows of seven, no drawn square cells, no grid lines. Below the LAST playable row, the very same platform widens gently into a front communication apron. Carve a broad softly irregular hollow into that apron, with a small portrait niche at its left and a readable message area beside it, two shallow thumb depressions along its lower lip. Show the character Nova portrait, the name "Nova", a short message "A little more room to breathe.", and action labels "Resume" and "Shower" engraved or lit on the stone. The portrait niche is physically inset, not a floating avatar bubble. Keep the lantern at the side of this connected apron. The entire communication hollow is below the usable arena, with no star behind it.

iPad landscape: recompose the same actual architecture for width instead of putting disconnected cards at far screen corners. Show one shallow broad moonstone terrace whose LEFT two thirds contain the same dominant 7x7 star arena. The right side of the platform grows into an organically connected crescent wing, from the SAME stone slab, with the message hollow physically carved into that wing. Score/control grooves are in the platform's own back/upper ledge, close to the arena. The right communication wing contains the inset Nova portrait and same brief native-text example/actions. Wide wallpaper clouds and quiet sky extend naturally beyond the platform on all sides. All UI recesses stay outside the 49-star arena. Both views feel like one crafted playable world with physically reserved interface pockets, not a HUD pasted on it.

Keep the star characters consistent with the current references, five distinct shapes/colors and readable faces, never circles around ordinary stars, never outline cell boxes. Do not introduce a central floor emblem, rune circle, logo, branding, health bars, cards, combat, timers, level counters or currencies. Crisp art-direction-quality painting, readable physical depth, high fidelity to the supplied game's cozy cosmic atmosphere. Prioritize the architectural grooves and the clear connected join to the platform over decorative complexity.
revision_prompt: Make ONE targeted correction to this Starfall phone/iPad environment concept. Preserve the entire phone view, every architectural groove, both message recesses, text, materials, telescope, clouds, lantern, lighting, composition and labels. The iPad landscape playfield at right currently has seven columns but only SIX rows of stars. Add its missing SEVENTH row just ABOVE the front stone rim and BELOW the current row that contains the large yellow star and purple dark star. The added row must contain exactly seven small stars, aligned with the existing seven columns, in this left-to-right order: yellow five-point, yellow five-point, yellow five-point, grey dark star, mint six-point, pink eight-point, aqua four-point. There is room in that foreground floor band, or adjust only row spacing slightly to fit. Keep every star safely on the uninterrupted arena floor and out of the score/message recesses. Final iPad board: exactly seven rows of seven stars, 49 total. Do not add grid lines, cell boxes, rings around ordinary stars, ornaments, UI cards or other content. Everything else must remain as close to the supplied image as possible.
notes: Native text/button regions are illustrated for communication only. Production art must omit text, glyphs and game pieces; native geometry and content remain authoritative.
